title: Linear hearing drift is not identified by bird survey turnover when observer cohort effects are free
abstract: We tested whether observer changes and song-frequency contrasts identify a linear hearing correction for bird climate tracking. We prove an exact equivalence between aging drift and observer cohort effects with a different calendar trend. We audit 130,303 standard Breeding Bird Survey runs on 5,319 routes in 1966-2025. Career and route tenure have no independent variation after observer-route and year effects. Aging and no-aging models give the same synthetic CTI means within 3.56e-15 C and the same turnover slope across 5,740 changes. Species-specific cohort effects can also preserve a song-frequency pattern. In a sensitivity model using rounded published slopes, an entry-cohort gradient of +0.005 CTI C per decade changes the corrected trend to zero. This is not an estimate of that gradient. The general age-period-cohort problem is established; the contribution is an explicit audit and sensitivity analysis of the thermal correction. The evidence supports a hearing mechanism but does not identify its linear correction without cohort restrictions or external detection data. We use schedule metadata and synthetic outcomes, not a new bird trend estimate.
